title: Check yourself: The window, context rot and trimming in code

questions.stem: A long agent session has thirty tool results, and the oldest twenty-five will never be needed again. What is the cheapest safe step?

options.text: Raise `max_tokens` so that the window can hold the older results as well
options.says: Ruled out because "more context isn't automatically better", and a larger limit does not remove the noise.

options.text: Delete the old results from the history and leave their calls in place without any reply
options.says: Ruled out because "Tool result blocks must immediately follow their corresponding tool use blocks in the message history."

options.text: Replace the whole conversation with one summary that a model writes for the agent
options.says: Ruled out because a summary "loses detail, so it comes last".

options.text: Swap the old outputs for a short placeholder, and keep every call in the history
options.says: The page says clearing "keeps both blocks and changes only the content of the result, so the pairing holds".

origin.section: Never split a call from its result

questions.stem: A program must drop old messages to fit a budget. What does the page say is the unit to drop?

options.text: A whole turn, which keeps each tool call together with its result
options.says: The page says "the unit of dropping is the turn", and that "A tool call and its result always sit in one turn."

options.text: A single message, starting with the oldest one in the list of messages
options.says: Ruled out because a message list that keeps a call and drops its result "fails with a 400 error".

options.text: One content block at a time, so that no passage of text is lost whole
options.says: Ruled out because "A tool call and its result always sit in one turn", so a block taken alone breaks the pair.

options.text: Every message that carries an image or a document, whatever its age
options.says: Ruled out because the functions "drop and fold whole turns only", whatever the content type.

origin.section: Never split a call from its result

questions.stem: Why is it a mistake to fill a 1M-token window as a matter of habit?

options.text: Cached prefixes do not count toward the window at all in the request
options.says: Ruled out because "all three count toward the window".

options.text: The API refuses any request that is over half of the window in size
options.says: Ruled out because the only refusal is when "the input alone is larger than the window".

options.text: Accuracy and recall both degrade as the amount of context grows
options.says: The page quotes "As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as *context rot*."

options.text: Output tokens are billed at the same price as input tokens
options.says: Ruled out because "The output counts too, including extended thinking." and the page names no price.
